scope: static read only; no source changes, Cargo, tests, native programs or new downloads
finding: no blocking issue identified in requested fresh-report, current-source binding and zero-run rejection scope
observations: Only eight Windows-specific OS path environment names plus explanatory comments were added to production .bazelrc; no forwarding of the whole runner environment.
Workflow binds checkout to source-head or actual PR merge commit, disables autocrlf via Git environment and sets an explicit expected commit for the wrapper.
Wrapper rejects non-Windows execution, unexpected HEAD, tracked source changes, missing exact env entries, and changed before/after source snapshots.
Existing target log and XML paths are deleted before --nocache_test_results run; each target requires exactly one fresh log and XML report.
XML requires one unfailed/unskipped Bazel wrapper and exact normalized log text; native summaries require full 33/35 outer counts with zero failed, ignored, measured or filtered tests.
The original one-test Git child with 32 filtered cases is required in its exact expected position and is not added to the outer denominator.
Zero test exits, skipped/cached target executions, missing lifecycle names and duplicate report wrappers cannot qualify under these explicit checks.
Command exit zero and literal two-out-of-two-executed summary are required in addition to original report parsing.
Historical retained reports serve parser controls only; current native qualification is not inferred from those controls.
limitations: No fresh Windows runner execution or actual nine parser control tests were run by this reviewer.
This review does not prove all Windows child-process security or semantics, nor all workspace CI acceptance.
Input snapshot and Git clean checks operate in the freshly checked-out workflow context; they are not a defense against a malicious Git/toolchain or arbitrary local environment.
